subject: Clarification request: pricing exhibit — price boundaries & packaging
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acmehealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — Order Form

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the draft order form. Our procurement team reviewed Exhibit B (Pricing Schedule) and flagged a couple of places that need clarity before we can present to our committee on Friday (9/10). High level items: 

- The definition of the "floor" is ambiguous — the exhibit alternately references per-SKU minimums and an aggregate monthly minimum. Which is controlling?
- Packaging tiers: the SKU mapping table doesn't explain how add-on bundles count toward the tier thresholds. For example, does the "Support Pack" bundle count as 1 SKU or does its constituent SKU lines add to volume?
- There's a short note about a "regional surcharge cap" but no example calculation. Our billing team needs the formula to model FY27 spend.

Attached is a short list of questions and a marked-up copy from procurement (Acme_Procurement_Questions.pdf). Can you provide a markup that: (1) fixes the floor definition to be explicit, (2) clarifies how bundles map to tier thresholds, and (3) provides an example surcharge calculation? Ideally we get something before EOD 9/7 so we can route to legal.

Appreciate it — if easier, we can hop on a 20-min call.

Best,
Elena Morris
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Health Systems

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-06T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — Order Form

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed notes and the marked-up PDF. Looping in Karthik (sales), Laura (legal) and Stephanie (finance) to help.

Quick responses:
- Our intention was that the "floor" in Exhibit B operates on aggregate monthly usage across SKUs unless a customer specifically elects per-SKU floors in the order schedule. That election language is probably too subtle in the current draft, so we'll make the controlling definition explicit.
- For packaging, the current model counts bundles as the sum of their constituent SKUs for tier math (i.e., the Support Pack contributes all underlying SKU volumes). If Acme would prefer treating bundles as atomic units for tiering we can add a carve-out.
- We'll add a one-line worked example for the regional surcharge cap and include the formula in the definition section.

Karthik — can you draft suggested language (and a short clause example) for the per-SKU vs aggregate floor? Laura, can you review once we have Karthik's suggested text so we can produce a redline for Acme? Stephanie, FYI in case we need to quantify the impact.

I attached an internal proposed markup (proposed_exhibit_markup_v1.docx) with my initial notes. Expect an updated redline by EOD 9/7.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Contracts & Pricing Ops
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Elena Morris <elena.morris@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — Order Form

Irene / Elena — attaching a short clause suggestion and the rationale. Bottom line proposal: make the default "aggregate monthly floor" explicit and add a single sentence that allows the customer to elect per-SKU floors ("Customer election"), which supersedes the default. Sample language below and in clause_suggestion.txt attachment.

--- sample clause snippet ---
"Floor; Calculation. Unless Customer elects the 'Per-SKU Floor' option in the Order Schedule, the Minimum Monthly Commitment (the 'Floor') shall be calculated on the basis of aggregate Paid Token-equivalent usage across all SKUs billed under this Order Form for each calendar month. If Customer elects 'Per-SKU Floor', the Minimum Monthly Commitment shall apply independently to each SKU listed in the Order Schedule."

For bundles: recommend we explicitly call out that bundles will count as the sum of underlying SKU quantities (so long as that is how Acme models consumption). If Acme wants to treat certain named bundles as atomic we can add an exception table in the order schedule.

Elena — is the atomic-bundle option something you'd want for Support Pack only, or for all bundles?

Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-08T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — Order Form

Thanks — that sample clause helps a lot. We discussed internally:

- We accept the default aggregate monthly floor for platform SKUs, but for regionally-billed professional services and certain compliance bundles (Support Pack), we need a per-region carve-out. Our spend model shows a meaningful mismatch if services are aggregated across regions.
- Regarding bundles: Support Pack should be treated as an atomic bundle for tiering (not summed). We can provide a short list of bundle SKUs that must be treated atomic.
- Regional surcharge calculation: please add an explicit formula and a worked numeric example to Exhibit B — we attached a small spreadsheet with three scenarios (high/med/low usage) so you can test the formula (usage-scenarios.xlsx).

If you can include the regional carve-out language and the surcharge example in a legal-ready redline, we can get legal signoff on 9/9. Otherwise our committee will likely request more edits which pushes the timeline.

Elena

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acmehealth.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-08T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on Pricing Exhibit — Order Form (legal redline attached)

Elena/Irene — thanks for the back-and-forth. I reviewed the proposed language and prepared a legal-ready markup that: (1) makes the aggregate-floor default explicit, (2) adds a clear 'Per-Region Carve-Out' subsection so that services billed by region can be carved out to per-region floors where listed in the Order Schedule, and (3) inserts the surcharge formula plus a worked numeric example.

Key points in the redline (exhibit_price_boundaries_redline.pdf attached):
- Section 3.1: "Minimum Monthly Commitment (Floor)" now states the controlling rule and the mechanics for Customer election.
- Section 3.4(b): "Per-Region Carve-Out" — requires the Order Schedule to list any SKUs or bundles to be treated per-region; absent a list, the aggregate default applies.
- Section 5.2: "Regional Surcharge Cap" — we added the calculation and three numeric example rows to mirror the spreadsheet Acme provided.

Next steps: Please review the attached redline. If Acme confirms the atomic-bundle list (Support Pack + Compliance Bundle), we can incorporate that into the Order Schedule and circulate for final signature via DocuSign. I added a one-click DocuSign route (link above). If Acme needs any wordsmithing, I'm available for a short call this afternoon. We aim to have a clean signature-ready Order Form by end of 9/9.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exhibit_price_boundaries_redline.pdf
